아이는 익숙한 사람과 장소에서는 과감해지고, 낯선 곳에서는 먼저 지켜봅니: Children are bold with familiar people and places and watch first in unfamiliar ones. The person who mostly sees them at home and the person who sees them at the playground or daycare see different sides.
자극에 대한 반응은 피곤하거나 배고플 때, 사람이 많을 때 더 크게 나타: Reactions to stimulation get bigger when tired, hungry or in crowds. The person who sees the morning rush and the person who sees bedtime may experience their sensitivity differently.
아이는 가장 편한 사람 앞에서 감정을 가장 크게 드러냅니다. 한 사람 앞: Children show their feelings most to the person they're most comfortable with. If they cry a lot only with one person, it may mean they feel safest with that person.
일과를 주로 챙기는 사람은 등원 준비나 잠자리처럼 전환이 어려운 순간을: The person who handles routines sees hard transitions like getting ready for daycare or bedtime more often, while the person who mostly plays with them sees their free side more often.
최근 처음 가 본 곳에서 아이가 처음 5분 동안 어떻게 했는지, 각자 본: Share the scenes you each saw of what your child did in their first 5 minutes somewhere new.
옷, 소리, 음식처럼 아이가 불편해한 순간이 언제였는지, 그때 아이의 컨: Compare notes on when your child was bothered by clothes, sounds or food, and how they were feeling at the time.
아이가 속상할 때 누구에게 먼저 가는지, 그때 각자 어떻게 반응하는지 이: Talk about who your child goes to first when upset, and how each of you responds.
아침 준비와 잠자리처럼 매일 반복되는 장면에서 각자 쓰는 방법을 비교하고: Compare how each of you handles daily scenes like getting ready in the morning and bedtime, and agree on the same order and words.
Persistence looks different depending on how hard the task is and how long the adult waits. Children persist less with someone who helps right away and more with someone who waits.
스스로 하는 모습은 시간이 넉넉할 때 잘 보입니다. 바쁜 아침을 맡는 사: Doing things alone shows best when there's plenty of time. Whoever handles busy mornings may rate it lower; whoever spends relaxed time with them may rate it higher.
또래와 있을 때, 형제와 있을 때, 어른과 있을 때 함께하는 모습은 서로: Getting along looks different with peers, siblings and adults. Think about who your child is usually with when each of you sees them.
아이 앞에서 서로의 방식을 고치지 않기: Don't correct each other's approach in front of your child
다르게 본 점은 아이가 없을 때 이야기합니다. 아이는 어른들의 의견이 갈: Talk about differences when your child isn't around. Children feel most anxious when the adults disagree.
같은 상황에는 같은 말 쓰기: Use the same words in the same situations
같은 방향으로 본 기질의 '잘 통하는 말'을 하나 골라, 모두 같은 문장: Pick one 'words that work' phrase from a trait you saw the same way, and all say it the same way.
한 달 뒤 다시 맞춰 보기: Check in again in a month
답이 갈린 장면을 한 달 동안 각자 지켜본 뒤 다시 이야기하면 차이가 좁: If you each watch the scenes where your answers differed for a month and talk again, the gap narrows.
새로운 것에 먼저 다가가는 모습이 늘었습니다. 익숙한 환경이 넓어졌거나: Approaching new things first has increased. Their familiar world may have grown, or they may be gaining confidence. Keep their eagerness alive, and agree on just one rule before starting.
먼저 지켜보는 모습이 늘었습니다. 새 기관, 새 친구처럼 낯선 일이 많았: Watching first has increased. This is common during periods with lots of new things, like a new daycare or new friends. Don't rush them; give them plenty of time to look around.
작은 변화에 더 민감해졌습니다. 잠이 부족하거나 환경이 바뀐 시기에 섬세: They've become more sensitive to small changes. Sensitivity can grow during periods of poor sleep or a changed environment. Reduce stimulation and make a quiet place to rest.
자극에 덜 흔들리게 되었습니다. 익숙해진 것이 늘고 스스로 진정하는 힘이: They're less shaken by stimulation now. It may be a sign that more things feel familiar and their ability to calm themselves has grown. Still, check now and then whether they're keeping discomfort to themselves.
감정을 더 크고 분명하게 드러냅니다. 말이 늘며 표현이 커지는 시기이거나: They're showing feelings bigger and more clearly. It may be a time when words and expression are growing, or something hard may have happened. Accept the feelings and just set limits on behavior.
감정을 안에서 다루는 모습이 늘었습니다. 스스로 조절하는 힘이 자란 것일: Handling feelings inside has increased. It may be growing self-control, or it may be holding back. Make time once a day to ask how they feel.
정해진 순서와 예고를 더 찾게 되었습니다. 일과가 자리 잡았거나, 변화가: They're looking for set order and warnings more. Their routine may have settled, or they may want predictability during a time of many changes. Tell them about changes in advance.
그때그때 흐름에 맞춰 움직이는 모습이 늘었습니다. 유연함이 자란 것일 수: Going with the flow has increased. Flexibility may have grown, or routines may have been disrupted. Set just two or three things that must be kept.
지난번과 비슷합니다. 기질은 타고난 바탕이라 몇 달 사이에 크게 바뀌지: Similar to last time. Temperament is an inborn base, so it's natural for it not to change much over a few months.
어려워도 다시 해 보는 경험이 쌓였습니다. 결과보다 다시 시도한 순간을: Experiences of trying again despite difficulty have added up. Praise the moments they tried again rather than the results.
요즘 과제가 어려워졌거나 피곤한 시기일 수 있습니다. 성공할 수 있는 쉬: Tasks may have gotten harder lately, or they may be tired. Lower the steps so they can succeed.
스스로 해 보려는 힘이 자랐습니다. 시간이 걸려도 기다려 주고, 아이가: Their drive to do things themselves has grown. Wait even if it takes time, and give them more things they can choose.
도움을 더 찾는 시기입니다. 동생이 생기거나 환경이 바뀌면 흔히 나타납니: They're seeking more help right now. This is common when a sibling arrives or things change. Give plenty of support, then hand back small tasks bit by bit.
함께 어울리는 힘이 자랐습니다. 차례 지키기, 나누기처럼 잘한 순간을 구: Their ability to get along has grown. Point out specific moments they did well, like taking turns or sharing.
또래와 갈등이 잦았거나 혼자 있고 싶은 시기일 수 있습니다. 소수의 친구: They may have had frequent conflicts with peers or want time alone. Start with short playtimes with a few friends.
